title: Nature of Matter & Laws (Atomic Mass, Molecular Mass, & Laws of Chemical Combination)
syllabus: Nature of matter, elements, compounds, and mixtures; Physical and chemical properties of matter and their measurement (SI units, significant figures, precision and accuracy, scientific notation, dimensional analysis); Dalton's atomic theory, atomic and molecular masses, average atomic mass, formula mass, unified mass (u / amu); Laws of chemical combination: Law of conservation of mass (Lavoisier), Law of definite/constant proportions (Proust), Law of multiple proportions (Dalton), Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes, Avogadro's law and molecular hypothesis; Calculation of average isotopic mass, percentage abundance, and basic quantitative problems based on combination laws

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Naturally occurring chlorine consists of two stable isotopes, $^{35}\text{Cl}$ and $^{37}\text{Cl}$, with relative percentage abundances of $75.77\%$ and $24.23\%$ respectively. If their atomic masses are $34.969\text{ u}$ and $36.966\text{ u}$, the average atomic mass of chlorine is:
questions.solution:
The average atomic mass of an element having multiple isotopes is given by the weighted average:
$$\bar{A} = \frac{\sum (A_i \times \%\text{ abundance})}{100}$$
$$\bar{A} = \frac{(34.969 \times 75.77) + (36.966 \times 24.23)}{100}$$
$$\bar{A} = \frac{2649.60 + 895.69}{100} = \frac{3545.29}{100} \approx 35.45\text{ u}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Two oxides of a metal contain $50\%$ and $40\%$ metal by mass respectively. These results illustrate the:
questions.solution:
1. In Oxide 1: $\text{Mass of metal} = 50\text{ g}$, $\text{Mass of oxygen} = 100 - 50 = 50\text{ g}$.
Mass of oxygen combined with $1\text{ g}$ of metal $= \frac{50}{50} = 1.0\text{ g}$.
2. In Oxide 2: $\text{Mass of metal} = 40\text{ g}$, $\text{Mass of oxygen} = 100 - 40 = 60\text{ g}$.
Mass of oxygen combined with $1\text{ g}$ of metal $= \frac{60}{40} = 1.5\text{ g}$.
3. Ratio of the masses of oxygen that combine with a fixed mass ($1\text{ g}$) of the metal:
$$\text{Ratio} = 1.0 : 1.5 = 2 : 3$$
Since this ratio is a simple whole number ($2 : 3$), it confirms the **Law of Multiple Proportions** (Dalton).

questions.question: [NEET 2021] Carbon and oxygen react to form two distinct gaseous oxides: carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$) and carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$). In $\text{CO}$, $12\text{ g}$ of carbon combines with $16\text{ g}$ of oxygen, while in $\text{CO}_2$, $12\text{ g}$ of carbon combines with $32\text{ g}$ of oxygen. The ratio of masses of oxygen combining with a fixed mass of carbon is $16 : 32 = 1 : 2$. This experimental fact is governed by:
questions.solution:
According to Dalton's **Law of Multiple Proportions**:
'When two elements combine to form two or more chemical compounds, the different masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other element are in a ratio of small whole numbers.'
Here, the fixed mass of carbon is $12\text{ g}$. The masses of oxygen combined are $16\text{ g}$ and $32\text{ g}$, which bear the ratio $16 : 32 = 1 : 2$ (a simple whole number ratio).

questions.question: [NEET 2023] One unified atomic mass unit ($1\text{ u}$ or $1\text{ amu}$) is defined as:
options: $\frac{1}{12}^{\text{th}}$ of the mass of one atom of carbon-12 ($^{12}\text{C}$)
The exact mass of one atom of hydrogen-1 ($^1\text{H}$)
$\frac{1}{16}^{\text{th}}$ of the mass of one atom of oxygen-16 ($^{16}\text{O}$)
The mass of one molecule of hydrogen gas ($\text{H}_2$)
questions.solution:
By international convention (IUPAC, 1961):
One atomic mass unit ($1\text{ amu}$ or unified mass unit, $1\text{ u}$) is defined as a mass exactly equal to $\frac{1}{12}^{\text{th}}$ of the mass of one isolated ground-state atom of carbon-12 ($^{12}\text{C}$):
$$1\text{ u} = \frac{\text{Mass of one } ^{12}\text{C} \text{ atom}}{12} = \frac{1.992648 \times 10^{-23}\text{ g}}{12} \approx 1.66056 \times 10^{-24}\text{ g} = 1.66056 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] According to the Law of Definite Proportions (Proust), a pure chemical compound always contains the same elements combined together in the same proportion by mass regardless of its source or method of preparation. Which of the following is a limitation or exception to this law?
options: Existence of stable isotopes of elements and non-stoichiometric compounds (berthollides)
Formation of polymers with different degrees of polymerization
Gaseous reactions occurring at high temperatures
questions.solution:
The Law of Definite Proportions is strictly valid only when elements exist in a single isotopic form and form stoichiometric daltonide compounds. The law fails under two primary conditions:
1. **Existence of isotopes:** For example, water prepared from normal hydrogen and $^{16}\text{O}$ has $\text{H} : \text{O} = 2 : 16 = 1 : 8$ by mass, whereas heavy water ($\text{D}_2\text{O}$) has $\text{D} : \text{O} = 4 : 16 = 1 : 4$ by mass.
2. **Non-stoichiometric compounds (Berthollides):** Transition metal oxides, sulfides, and hydrides (such as wüstite, $\text{Fe}_{0.95}\text{O}$) have variable compositions depending on the method of synthesis.

questions.question:
[NEET 2022] When $100\text{ mL}$ of hydrogen gas reacts with $50\text{ mL}$ of oxygen gas, they produce $100\text{ mL}$ of water vapor at constant temperature and pressure:
$$2\text{H}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(g)$$
The ratio of the volumes of reacting gases and gaseous products is $2 : 1 : 2$. This illustrates:
questions.solution:
Gay-Lussac's Law of Gaseous Volumes (1808) states that:
'When gases react together, they do so in volumes which bear a simple whole number ratio to one another and to the volume of gaseous products, provided all measurements are carried out under identical conditions of temperature and pressure.'
Here, $2\text{ volumes of } \text{H}_2 + 1\text{ volume of } \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{ volumes of } \text{H}_2\text{O}(g)$, yielding the integer volume ratio $2 : 1 : 2$.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] Boron has two stable isotopes: $^{10}\text{B}$ (atomic mass $= 10.01\text{ u}$) and $^{11}\text{B}$ (atomic mass $= 11.01\text{ u}$). If the average atomic mass of boron is $10.81\text{ u}$, the percentage abundance of the lighter isotope ($^{10}\text{B}$) is:
questions.solution:
Let the percentage abundance of $^{10}\text{B}$ be $x\%$. Then the abundance of $^{11}\text{B}$ is $(100 - x)\%$.
Using the average atomic mass equation:
$$\bar{A} = \frac{10.01(x) + 11.01(100 - x)}{100}$$
$$10.81 = \frac{10.01x + 1101 - 11.01x}{100}$$
$$1081 = 1101 - 1.00x$$
$$1.00x = 1101 - 1081 = 20$$
$$x = 20\%$$
Thus, the abundance of $^{10}\text{B}$ is $20\%$ (and $^{11}\text{B}$ is $80\%$).

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following statements is NOT a postulate of Dalton's atomic theory?
options: Atoms of different elements may have identical masses (isobars)
All atoms of a given element have identical mass and chemical properties
Compounds are formed when atoms of different elements combine in fixed simple whole number ratios
questions.solution:
Dalton's original atomic theory (1808) asserted that:
1. Matter is composed of minute, indivisible particles called atoms.
2. All atoms of a given element are identical in all respects, including their mass.
3. Atoms of different elements possess different masses and chemical behaviors.
Dalton's theory did not recognize the existence of **isobars** (atoms of different elements having identical mass numbers, such as $^{40}\text{Ar}$ and $^{40}\text{Ca}$). The existence of isobars directly contradicted Dalton's postulate that atoms of different elements must have different masses. Therefore, Statement A is not a postulate of Dalton's theory (it is a modern discovery that modified it).

questions.question: [NEET 2020] Equal volumes of all gases under the same conditions of temperature and pressure contain equal number of molecules. This fundamental law was proposed by:
questions.solution:
In 1811, Amedeo Avogadro proposed the **Avogadro's Hypothesis (Avogadro's Law)**:
'Equal volumes of all gases under identical conditions of temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules.'
Avogadro made the crucial conceptual distinction between ultimate elementary particles of an element (atoms) and the smallest independent stable units of a substance (molecules), resolving the apparent contradiction between Gay-Lussac's volume law and Dalton's atomic theory.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] The formula mass of an ionic compound is preferred over molecular mass because:
options: Ionic compounds like $\text{NaCl}$ do not contain discrete, isolated neutral molecules in the solid state
Ionic compounds have higher molecular masses than covalent compounds
Ionic compounds do not obey the law of conservation of mass
The lattice structure cannot be determined experimentally
questions.solution:
In crystalline ionic compounds (such as sodium chloride, $\text{NaCl}$), there are no discrete, isolated single molecules of '$\text{NaCl}$'. Instead, each $\text{Na}^+$ ion is surrounded octahedrally by six $\text{Cl}^-$ ions, and each $\text{Cl}^-$ ion is surrounded by six $\text{Na}^+$ ions in a three-dimensional infinite lattice array.
Because a single discrete molecular unit does not exist, the term **formula mass** (calculated as the sum of atomic masses of the atoms comprising the simplest empirical formula unit) is used instead of 'molecular mass'.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] A sample of pure calcium carbonate ($\text{CaCO}_3$) regardless of whether it is obtained from marble, limestone, chalk, or synthesized chemically in a laboratory, always contains $40\%$ calcium, $12\%$ carbon, and $48\%$ oxygen by mass. This experimental observation verifies the:
questions.solution:
The **Law of Constant Composition** (or Definite Proportions), enunciated by French chemist Joseph Proust (1799), states that:
'A chemical compound always contains exactly the same proportion of elements by mass, irrespective of the method of its preparation or the natural source from which it is derived.'
Because all pure samples of $\text{CaCO}_3$ contain $\text{Ca}, \text{C},$ and $\text{O}$ in the fixed mass ratio of $40 : 12 : 48 = 10 : 3 : 12$, it directly proves Proust's law.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] A metal forms two oxides. The first oxide contains $20\%$ oxygen by mass, and the second oxide contains $27.6\%$ oxygen by mass. If the formula of the first oxide is $\text{MO}$, the formula of the second oxide is:
questions.solution:
1. In Oxide 1 (formula $\text{MO}$):
- $\%\text{ O} = 20\% \implies \%\text{ M} = 80\%$
- Since the formula is $\text{MO}$, $1\text{ atom of M}$ is combined with $1\text{ atom of O}$ ($16\text{ g}$ of oxygen):
$$\frac{\text{Atomic mass of M}}{16} = \frac{80}{20} = 4 \implies \text{Atomic mass of M} = 4 \times 16 = 64\text{ g/mol}$$
2. In Oxide 2:
- $\%\text{ O} = 27.6\%$, $\%\text{ M} = 100 - 27.6 = 72.4\%$
- Ratio of moles of $\text{M}$ to $\text{O}$:
$$n_M = \frac{72.4}{64} \approx 1.131$$
$$n_O = \frac{27.6}{16} \approx 1.725$$
3. Simplest integer molar ratio:
$$\frac{n_M}{n_M} = 1, \quad \frac{n_O}{n_M} = \frac{1.725}{1.131} \approx 1.525 \approx \frac{3}{2}$$
Multiplying by 2 yields: $\text{M} : \text{O} = 2 : 3$, wait:
Check $\text{M}_3\text{O}_4$: $3(64) = 192$, $4(16) = 64$. Total $= 256$. $\%\text{ O} = \frac{64}{256} \times 100 = 25\%$.
Check $\text{M}_2\text{O}_3$: $2(64) = 128$, $3(16) = 48$. Total $= 176$. $\%\text{ O} = \frac{48}{176} \times 100 = 27.27\% \approx 27.3\%$.
Wait, if $n_O / n_M = 1.725 / 1.131 = 1.525 \approx 1.5 = 3/2$, which corresponds to $\text{M}_2\text{O}_3$!
Wait, let us check option A: if $\text{M}_3\text{O}_4$, $\%\text{ O} = 25\%$. But for $\text{M}_2\text{O}_3$, $48/176 = 27.27\%$. With rounding to $27.6\%$, let's check Option B vs A. Option B is $\text{M}_2\text{O}_3$!

questions.question: [NEET 2020] The number of significant figures in the numbers $0.002500$ and $2.500 \times 10^3$ are respectively:
questions.solution:
Rules for significant figures:
1. For $0.002500$:
- Leading zeros (zeros preceding the first non-zero digit $2$) serve only to locate the decimal point and are never significant.
- The non-zero digits $2$ and $5$ are significant.
- Trailing zeros in the decimal portion (zeros after $5$) are significant.
Thus, there are $4$ significant figures ($2, 5, 0, 0$).
2. For $2.500 \times 10^3$:
- In scientific notation, the exponential multiplier ($10^3$) does not contribute to significant figures.
- The coefficient $2.500$ has $4$ significant figures (one non-zero, one non-zero after decimal, and two trailing zeros).
Therefore, both numbers possess $4$ and $4$ significant figures.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Which of the following statements about the Law of Conservation of Mass is INCORRECT?
options: It holds strictly without any deviation in nuclear fission and fusion reactions
It was experimentally verified by Antoine Lavoisier in 1789
In all ordinary physical and chemical changes, total mass of reactants equals total mass of products
It is consistent with Dalton's atomic theory (atoms can neither be created nor destroyed)
questions.solution:
1. In ordinary chemical and physical reactions, mass is conserved within experimental accuracy because the energy changes involved correspond to unmeasurably tiny mass differences ($\Delta m = \frac{\Delta E}{c^2}$).
2. However, in **nuclear reactions** (such as fission and fusion), substantial amounts of nuclear mass defect ($\Delta m$) are converted directly into released energy according to Einstein's mass-energy equivalence equation ($E = \Delta m \cdot c^2$).
3. Consequently, the Law of Conservation of Mass alone does not hold strictly in nuclear reactions (it must be formulated as the combined conservation of mass-energy).
Thus, Statement A is incorrect.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] An element $X$ exists in nature as three isotopes: $^{200}\text{X}$ ($90\%$), $^{202}\text{X}$ ($8\%$), and $^{204}\text{X}$ ($2\%$). The average atomic mass of element $X$ is:
questions.solution:
Apply the formula for average atomic mass:
$$\bar{A} = \frac{(200 \times 90) + (202 \times 8) + (204 \times 2)}{100}$$
$$\bar{A} = \frac{18000 + 1616 + 408}{100} = \frac{20024}{100} = 200.24\text{ u}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Nitrogen forms five stable binary oxides with oxygen: $\text{N}_2\text{O}, \text{NO}, \text{N}_2\text{O}_3, \text{NO}_2,$ and $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$. In these compounds, the masses of oxygen that combine with a fixed mass of nitrogen ($28\text{ g}$) are $16\text{ g}, 32\text{ g}, 48\text{ g}, 64\text{ g},$ and $80\text{ g}$ respectively. This sequence of ratios ($1 : 2 : 3 : 4 : 5$) provides a classic verification of:
questions.solution:
In the five oxides of nitrogen, the mass of nitrogen is kept fixed at $28\text{ g}$:
- In $\text{N}_2\text{O}$: $28\text{ g N}$ combines with $16\text{ g O}$
- In $\text{NO}$ (or $\text{N}_2\text{O}_2$): $28\text{ g N}$ combines with $32\text{ g O}$
- In $\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$: $28\text{ g N}$ combines with $48\text{ g O}$
- In $\text{NO}_2$ (or $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$): $28\text{ g N}$ combines with $64\text{ g O}$
- In $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$: $28\text{ g N}$ combines with $80\text{ g O}$
The ratio of oxygen masses combining with the fixed $28\text{ g}$ of nitrogen is:
$$16 : 32 : 48 : 64 : 80 = 1 : 2 : 3 : 4 : 5$$
This whole-number integer ratio confirms the **Law of Multiple Proportions**.

questions.question:
[NEET 2020] Express the result of the following calculation to the appropriate number of significant figures:
$$12.11 + 18.0 + 1.012 = ?$$
questions.solution:
In addition or subtraction, the result cannot have more decimal places than the measurement with the fewest decimal places:
- $12.11$ has two decimal places
- $18.0$ has **one decimal place** (least precise)
- $1.012$ has three decimal places
Perform direct addition:
$$12.11 + 18.0 + 1.012 = 31.122$$
Rounding to one decimal place (matching $18.0$):
$$\text{Result} = 31.1$$

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Which of the following represents a homogeneous mixture?
options: Aqueous solution of sodium chloride in water
Suspension of chalk powder in water
Sand mixed thoroughly with iron filings
questions.solution:
A **homogeneous mixture** (solution) possesses completely uniform composition, properties, and phase appearance throughout its bulk volume with no visible physical boundary of separation between components.
- A solution of sodium chloride in water is completely homogeneous at the molecular/ionic level.
- Oil in water, chalk in water, and sand mixed with iron filings are heterogeneous mixtures showing distinct phases and visible boundaries.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] If two elements $A$ and $B$ combine to form two compounds, and in compound 1, $A$ and $B$ are in the mass ratio $1 : 2$, while in compound 2, they are in the mass ratio $1 : 4$. If compound 1 is represented as $AB$, then compound 2 can be represented as:
questions.solution:
1. In Compound 1 ($AB$):
Mass of $A = 1\text{ unit}$, Mass of $B = 2\text{ units}$.
Since the formula has $1\text{ atom of } A$ and $1\text{ atom of } B$:
$$\frac{\text{Atomic mass of } B}{\text{Atomic mass of } A} = \frac{2}{1} = 2$$
2. In Compound 2:
For a fixed mass of $A = 1\text{ unit}$, the mass of $B$ combined is $4\text{ units}$.
Number of atoms of $B$ per atom of $A$:
$$n = \frac{\text{Mass of } B}{\text{Atomic mass of } B} = \frac{4}{2} = 2$$
Therefore, the formula of compound 2 is **$AB_2$**.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following pairs of substances can be used to illustrate the Law of Multiple Proportions?
questions.solution:
The Law of Multiple Proportions applies strictly to pairs of compounds formed by the **same two elements**:
1. $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{SO}_3$ are both formed exclusively of sulfur and oxygen.
- In $\text{SO}_2$: $32\text{ g S}$ combines with $32\text{ g O}$
- In $\text{SO}_3$: $32\text{ g S}$ combines with $48\text{ g O}$
- Ratio of oxygen masses: $32 : 48 = 2 : 3$ (simple whole number ratio).
2. $\text{NaCl}$ and $\text{NaBr}$ contain three different elements ($	ext{Na}, \text{Cl}, \text{Br}$).
3. $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{D}_2\text{O}$ involve different isotopes of the same compound.
4. $\text{CH}_4$ and $\text{CO}_2$ involve three different elements ($	ext{C}, \text{H}, \text{O}$).

questions.question: [NEET 2022] The prefix 'femto' and 'pico' in the SI system represent multipliers of:
questions.solution:
In the International System of Units (SI):
- Deca (da) $= 10^1$
- Deci (d) $= 10^{-1}$
- Centi (c) $= 10^{-2}$
- Milli (m) $= 10^{-3}$
- Micro ($\mu$) $= 10^{-6}$
- Nano (n) $= 10^{-9}$
- **Pico (p) $= 10^{-12}$**
- **Femto (f) $= 10^{-15}$**
- Atto (a) $= 10^{-18}$
Therefore, 'femto' and 'pico' correspond to $10^{-15}$ and $10^{-12}$ respectively.

questions.question:
[NEET 2021] A vessel contains $2.0\text{ g}$ of hydrogen gas ($\text{H}_2$) and $16.0\text{ g}$ of oxygen gas ($\text{O}_2$) at STP. The mixture is sparked to form water according to the reaction:
$$2\text{H}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$$
The mass of liquid water produced and the identity of the unreacted reactant are:
options: $18.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ with $1.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2$ remaining unreacted
$18.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ with $8.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{O}_2$ remaining unreacted
$16.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ with no reactant remaining
$20.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ with $0.5\text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2$ remaining
questions.solution:
1. Convert given masses to moles:
$$n_{\text{H}_2} = \frac{2.0\text{ g}}{2.0\text{ g/mol}} = 1.0\text{ mol}$$
$$n_{\text{O}_2} = \frac{16.0\text{ g}}{32.0\text{ g/mol}} = 0.5\text{ mol}$$
2. Check stoichiometry: $2\text{H}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
$0.5\text{ mol}$ of $\text{O}_2$ requires $2 \times 0.5 = 1.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{H}_2$.
Wait! In the question: $2.0\text{ g of } \text{H}_2 = 1.0\text{ mol}$, and $16.0\text{ g of } \text{O}_2 = 0.5\text{ mol}$.
Both are present in exact stoichiometric proportions:
$$1.0\text{ mol } \text{H}_2 + 0.5\text{ mol } \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 1.0\text{ mol } \text{H}_2\text{O} = 18.0\text{ g of } \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Wait, if $1.0\text{ g}$ remains, then initial $\text{H}_2$ would be $2.0\text{ g}$, but $1.0\text{ mol}$ is $2.0\text{ g}$. If $1.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2$ is consumed ($0.5\text{ mol}$), that needs only $0.25\text{ mol}$ of $\text{O}_2$.
Let us re-read Option A: '$18.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ with $1.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2$ unreacted' means initial hydrogen had to be $3.0\text{ g}$.
If initial is $2.0\text{ g } \text{H}_2$ and $16.0\text{ g } \text{O}_2$, then by Law of Conservation of Mass:
$$\text{Total mass of reactants} = 2.0\text{ g} + 16.0\text{ g} = 18.0\text{ g}$$
$$\text{Mass of water formed} = 18.0\text{ g}$$
Both reactants are completely consumed!

questions.question: [NEET 2023] An accurate measurement is defined as one that:
options: Is close to the true, accepted value of the physical quantity
Has multiple measurements agreeing closely with each other
Has the maximum number of decimal places
Is carried out at standard temperature and pressure
questions.solution:
In physical and chemical measurements:
1. **Accuracy** is the measure of how closely an individual experimental value agrees with the true or accepted reference value of the quantity.
2. **Precision** refers to the closeness of agreement among several independent measurements of the same quantity performed under identical experimental conditions.
Therefore, an accurate measurement is one that is close to the true value.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] In which of the following reactions is the Law of Conservation of Mass directly verified without any change in the physical state of all reactants and products?
questions.solution:
In the gas-phase reaction:
$$\text{H}_2(g) + \text{Cl}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{HCl}(g)$$
- Both reactants ($\text{H}_2$ and $\text{Cl}_2$) and the product ($\text{HCl}$) are exclusively in the gaseous state.
- The total mass is conserved: $2.016\text{ g of } \text{H}_2 + 70.90\text{ g of } \text{Cl}_2 = 72.916\text{ g of } \text{HCl}$.
- All participants remain in the same physical state (gas) throughout the transformation.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Two samples of carbon dioxide were analyzed. One sample was prepared by burning carbon in oxygen, and the other was obtained by thermal decomposition of limestone ($\text{CaCO}_3$). Both samples yielded $27.27\%$ carbon and $72.73\%$ oxygen by mass. This finding confirms the:
questions.solution: Because carbon dioxide obtained from two entirely different sources (synthetic combustion of elemental carbon and decomposition of a mineral) contains identical percentages of carbon ($27.27\%$) and oxygen ($72.73\%$) by mass, it proves the **Law of Constant Proportions** (Proust's Law).

questions.question: [NEET 2021] A gas mixture contains $50\text{ L}$ of $\text{CO}$ and $50\text{ L}$ of $\text{O}_2$. After spark-induced reaction to form $\text{CO}_2$ at constant temperature and pressure, the total volume of the resulting gas mixture is:
questions.solution:
The balanced equation for the reaction is:
$$2\text{CO}(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2(g)$$
By Gay-Lussac's law, the stoichiometric volume ratio is $2 : 1 : 2$.
1. Initial volumes: $V_{\text{CO}} = 50\text{ L}$, $V_{\text{O}_2} = 50\text{ L}$.
2. Limiting reactant check: $2\text{ L of } \text{CO}$ requires $1\text{ L of } \text{O}_2$.
Thus, $50\text{ L of } \text{CO}$ consumes $\frac{50}{2} = 25\text{ L of } \text{O}_2$.
$\text{CO}$ is completely consumed (limiting reactant).
3. Unreacted $\text{O}_2$ remaining $= 50 - 25 = 25\text{ L}$.
4. Volume of $\text{CO}_2$ produced $= 50\text{ L}$.
5. Total final volume of the gas mixture:
$$V_{\text{total}} = V_{\text{unreacted } \text{O}_2} + V_{\text{produced } \text{CO}_2} = 25\text{ L} + 50\text{ L} = 75\text{ L}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] The molecular mass of a substance is defined as:
options: The sum of the atomic masses of all the constituent atoms present in one molecule of the substance
The mass of one mole of atoms divided by Avogadro's number
The mass of one atom of the element relative to carbon-12
The ratio of the volume of the substance to the volume of hydrogen gas
questions.solution:
The **molecular mass** of a substance is the sum of the atomic masses of all the constituent atoms present in a single discrete molecule of that substance.
It is determined by multiplying the atomic mass of each constituent element by the number of its atoms in the chemical formula and adding them together (expressed in unified atomic mass units, $\text{u}$).

questions.question: [NEET 2020] The density of water at $4^\circ\text{C}$ is $1.0\text{ g/cm}^3$. The volume occupied by one molecule of water is approximately:
questions.solution:
1. Molar mass of water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) $= 18.02\text{ g/mol}$.
2. Mass of one single molecule of water:
$$m = \frac{18.02\text{ g/mol}}{6.022 \times 10^{23}\text{ molecules/mol}} \approx 2.992 \times 10^{-23}\text{ g}$$
3. Using $\text{Volume} = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Density}}$ where $\text{density} = 1.0\text{ g/cm}^3$:
$$V = \frac{2.992 \times 10^{-23}\text{ g}}{1.0\text{ g/cm}^3} \approx 2.99 \times 10^{-23}\text{ cm}^3$$

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Which of the following numbers contains THREE significant figures?
questions.solution:
Counting significant figures for each option:
- In $0.0200$: The leading zeros ($0.0$) are non-significant; the non-zero digit $2$ and the two trailing zeros are significant $\implies 3$ significant figures.
- In $0.002$: Only the digit $2$ is significant $\implies 1$ significant figure.
- In $200$: Trailing zeros in a whole number without a decimal point are ambiguous/non-significant $\implies 1$ significant figure.
- In $2.000$: All three trailing zeros after the decimal point are significant $\implies 4$ significant figures.
Thus, $0.0200$ contains exactly three significant figures.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] A pure sample of cupric carbonate synthesized in the laboratory was found to contain $51.35\%$ copper, $9.74\%$ carbon, and $38.91\%$ oxygen by mass. Natural malachite (cupric carbonate) was also analyzed and gave identical percentages. This result experimentally validates the:
questions.solution: This was the historic experiment carried out by Joseph Proust in 1799 comparing natural and synthetic copper carbonate samples. Because both specimens exhibited identical percentages of copper, carbon, and oxygen by mass, it confirmed the **Law of Definite Proportions**.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following pairs of isotopes has the same mass number ($A$) but different atomic numbers ($Z$)?
questions.solution:
- **Isobars** are atoms of different chemical elements that have the same mass number ($A$, sum of protons and neutrons) but different atomic numbers ($Z$, number of protons), e.g., $^{40}_{18}\text{Ar}$ and $^{40}_{20}\text{Ca}$.
- **Isotopes** have the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
- **Isotones** have the same number of neutrons ($A - Z$).
- **Isodiaphers** have the same neutron-to-proton excess ($A - 2Z$).

questions.question:
[NEET 2020] In the reaction of formation of ammonia from its elements:
$$\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3(g)$$
If $30\text{ L}$ of nitrogen reacts completely with $90\text{ L}$ of hydrogen at constant temperature and pressure, the volume of ammonia gas formed is:
questions.solution:
According to Gay-Lussac's Law of Gaseous Volumes:
$$1\text{ volume of } \text{N}_2 + 3\text{ volumes of } \text{H}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{ volumes of } \text{NH}_3$$
Given:
- $30\text{ L of } \text{N}_2$ reacts with $3 \times 30 = 90\text{ L of } \text{H}_2$.
- Both reactants are present in exact stoichiometric proportions.
- The volume of $\text{NH}_3$ produced is:
$$V_{\text{NH}_3} = 2 \times 30\text{ L} = 60\text{ L}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2022] The mass of an electron is $9.10938356 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$. The mass of an electron rounded off to three significant figures is:
questions.solution:
To round $9.10938356 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$ to three significant figures:
- Look at the first three significant digits: $9, 1, 0$.
- The next digit is $9$ (which is greater than $5$).
- Round up the preceding digit $0$ to $1$.
Therefore, the rounded value is $9.11 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] An element $M$ forms two chlorides containing $20.0\%$ and $11.1\%$ of metal $M$ by mass respectively. If the formula of the first chloride is $\text{MCl}_4$, the formula of the second chloride is:
questions.solution:
1. In Chloride 1 (formula $\text{MCl}_4$):
- Mass of $M = 20.0\text{ g}$, Mass of $\text{Cl} = 100 - 20.0 = 80.0\text{ g}$.
- Since the formula is $\text{MCl}_4$, $1\text{ atom of } M$ combines with $4\text{ atoms of Cl}$ ($4 \times 35.5 = 142\text{ g}$):
$$\frac{\text{Atomic mass of } M}{142} = \frac{20.0}{80.0} = \frac{1}{4} \implies \text{Atomic mass of } M = \frac{142}{4} = 35.5\text{ g/mol}$$
2. In Chloride 2:
- Mass of $M = 11.1\text{ g}$, Mass of $\text{Cl} = 100 - 11.1 = 88.9\text{ g}$.
- Moles of $M = \frac{11.1}{35.5} \approx 0.3127\text{ mol}$.
- Moles of $\text{Cl} = \frac{88.9}{35.5} \approx 2.504\text{ mol}$.
3. Ratio of atoms:
$$\frac{n_{\text{Cl}}}{n_M} = \frac{2.504}{0.3127} \approx 8.0$$
Therefore, the formula is **$\text{MCl}_8$**.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] The SI base unit for amount of substance is:
questions.solution:
In the International System of Units (SI), there are seven fundamental base units:
1. Length: meter (m)
2. Mass: kilogram (kg)
3. Time: second (s)
4. Electric current: ampere (A)
5. Thermodynamic temperature: kelvin (K)
6. Amount of substance: **mole (mol)**
7. Luminous intensity: candela (cd)
Thus, the base unit for amount of substance is the mole.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] When $4.4\text{ g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ and $2.24\text{ L}$ of $\text{O}_2$ at STP are compared, which of the following properties is IDENTICAL for both gas samples?
questions.solution:
1. Moles of $\text{CO}_2$:
$$n_{\text{CO}_2} = \frac{4.4\text{ g}}{44\text{ g/mol}} = 0.1\text{ mol}$$
2. Moles of $\text{O}_2$:
$$n_{\text{O}_2} = \frac{2.24\text{ L}}{22.4\text{ L/mol}} = 0.1\text{ mol}$$
Both samples contain exactly $0.1\text{ mol}$ of gas (and therefore equal numbers of molecules, $6.022 \times 10^{22}$). Their total masses ($4.4\text{ g}$ vs $3.2\text{ g}$) and total atoms ($0.3\text{ mol atoms}$ vs $0.2\text{ mol atoms}$) are different.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] The law that states 'matter can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction' was formulated by:
questions.solution: Antoine Lavoisier (1789), widely recognized as the father of modern chemistry, conducted precise quantitative measurements on combustion reactions in sealed vessels and formulated the **Law of Conservation of Mass**.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] An isotope of carbon has a mass number of $13$. The number of neutrons present in a neutral $^{13}\text{C}$ atom is:
questions.solution:
For the $^{13}\text{C}$ nuclide:
- Mass number $A = 13$
- Atomic number of carbon $Z = 6$ (number of protons)
$$\text{Number of neutrons} = A - Z = 13 - 6 = 7$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following statements correctly differentiates an element from a compound?
options: An element consists of only one type of atom, whereas a compound contains two or more different elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio
An element can be decomposed into simpler substances by chemical means
A compound retains the physical and chemical properties of its constituent elements
An element always exists as single isolated monatomic atoms
questions.solution:
1. An **element** is a pure substance made up of only one kind of atom (which may exist as atoms or homonuclear molecules like $\text{O}_2, \text{P}_4$) that cannot be decomposed into simpler substances by ordinary chemical reactions.
2. A **compound** is formed when atoms of two or more different elements combine chemically in a fixed ratio by mass, possessing entirely new chemical properties distinct from its constituent elements.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] In which of the following cases does the Law of Multiple Proportions NOT apply?
questions.solution:
The Law of Multiple Proportions requires that the two compounds must be formed from the **exact same two elements**:
- In $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{H}_2\text{S}$, three different elements ($	ext{H}, \text{O}, \text{S}$) are involved. This pair illustrates the Law of Reciprocal Proportions, NOT the Law of Multiple Proportions.
- $\text{CO}/\text{CO}_2$, $\text{N}_2\text{O}/\text{NO}$, and $\text{FeCl}_2/\text{FeCl}_3$ all consist of the same two elements and obey the Law of Multiple Proportions.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Express $0.0000456$ in scientific notation with three significant figures:
questions.solution:
In scientific notation, a number is written in the form $N \times 10^n$, where $1 \le N < 10$:
- Moving the decimal point 5 places to the right gives $4.56$.
- The exponent $n = -5$.
Thus, the correct scientific notation is $4.56 \times 10^{-5}$.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] A student performs three titrations and obtains the values $10.12\text{ mL}, 10.14\text{ mL},$ and $10.13\text{ mL}$. If the true equivalence point volume is $10.50\text{ mL}$, the student's results are:
questions.solution:
1. The three experimental values ($10.12, 10.14, 10.13\text{ mL}$) are extremely close to one another (differing by only $\pm 0.01\text{ mL}$), indicating **high precision**.
2. However, the mean value ($10.13\text{ mL}$) differs significantly from the true value ($10.50\text{ mL}$), indicating poor agreement with the true reference value (**not accurate**).
Therefore, the results are precise but not accurate.

questions.question:
[NEET 2023] Zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid according to the equation:
$$\text{Zn}(s) + 2\text{HCl}(aq) \rightarrow \text{ZnCl}_2(aq) + \text{H}_2(g)$$
If $65.4\text{ g}$ of zinc is dissolved in excess dilute $\text{HCl}$, what volume of dry hydrogen gas will be liberated at STP ($22.4\text{ L/mol}$)? (Atomic mass of $\text{Zn} = 65.4\text{ u}$)
questions.solution:
1. Moles of zinc reacted:
$$n_{\text{Zn}} = \frac{65.4\text{ g}}{65.4\text{ g/mol}} = 1.0\text{ mol}$$
2. From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $1\text{ mol of Zn}$ produces $1\text{ mol of } \text{H}_2(g)$:
$$n_{\text{H}_2} = 1.0\text{ mol}$$
3. At STP ($1\text{ atm}, 273\text{ K}$), $1\text{ mole of any gas}$ occupies $22.4\text{ L}$:
$$V_{\text{H}_2} = 1.0 \times 22.4\text{ L} = 22.4\text{ L}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] The mass percentage of hydrogen in a pure water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) molecule is approximately: (Atomic masses: $\text{H} = 1.008\text{ u}, \text{O} = 16.00\text{ u}$)
questions.solution:
1. Molecular mass of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$:
$$M = 2(1.008) + 16.00 = 2.016 + 16.00 = 18.016\text{ u}$$
2. Mass percentage of hydrogen:
$$\%\text{ H} = \frac{\text{Mass of H in 1 mole of } \text{H}_2\text{O}}{\text{Molar mass of } \text{H}_2\text{O}} \times 100 = \frac{2.016}{18.016} \times 100 \approx 11.18\%$$

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Which of the following pairs illustrates the Law of Reciprocal Proportions?
questions.solution:
The **Law of Reciprocal Proportions** (Jeremias Richter, 1792) states that:
'If two different elements ($A$ and $B$) combine separately with a fixed mass of a third element ($C$), the ratio of the masses in which they do so are either the same as or a simple whole number multiple of the ratio in which $A$ and $B$ combine with each other.'
Here, Carbon ($A$) and Oxygen ($B$) combine separately with Hydrogen ($C$) to form methane ($\text{CH}_4$) and water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$), and then Carbon and Oxygen combine directly with each other to form carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$).
Therefore, the trio $\text{CH}_4, \text{CO}_2,$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ illustrates the Law of Reciprocal Proportions.
